Completion time for both tasks: how long participants spent on each trial page, by
visualization type, and (for Task 1) how time relates to accuracy.

```{r time-rule-and-helpers}
#| include: false
# ---- Outlier rule (one rule for every table, figure and model) ----------------
# A trial page open for longer than this is treated as an interruption and
# excluded. The cap is fixed in seconds, not estimated from the data.
time_cap_sec <- 180
apply_time_rule <- function(df) dplyr::filter(df, time_sec <= time_cap_sec)

# ---- Times per trial page -------------------------------------------------------
# "Time spent on page xxx": a trial page keeps its questionnaire number when the
# display order is randomized, so page number - offset = trial number.
read_page_times <- function(first_var, last_var, offset, trials) {
  data %>%
    select(ID, all_of(first_var):all_of(last_var)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-ID, names_to = "time_var", values_to = "time_sec") %>%
    mutate(
      ID = as.character(ID),
      trial = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(time_var, "TIME")) - offset,
      time_sec = readr::parse_double(as.character(time_sec))
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      trials %>%
        transmute(ID = as.character(ID), trial, position, vistype),
      by = c("ID", "trial")
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(time_sec), !is.na(vistype), time_sec > 0)
}

# ---- Time model -----------------------------------------------------------------
# log(time) mixed model. Back-transformed estimates are geometric means for a
# typical participant (random intercept at zero) at the average position.
# Differences from Basic are ratios of geometric means, Dunnett-adjusted
# (emmeans "mvt", exact multivariate t, six comparisons with Basic topoplot).
# Degrees of freedom are asymptotic for every fit: emmeans would otherwise switch
# to Kenward-Roger below 3,000 trials (e.g. the IQR sensitivity fit).
ci_bounds <- function(df) {
  lower <- intersect(c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"), names(df))
  upper <- intersect(c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"), names(df))
  stopifnot(length(lower) == 1L, length(upper) == 1L)
  list(lower = df[[lower]], upper = df[[upper]])
}

fit_time_model <- function(time_data) {
  model_data <- time_data %>%
    transmute(
      ID = factor(ID),
      vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
      position = as.integer(position),
      time_sec = as.numeric(time_sec)
    ) %>%
    filter(complete.cases(.), time_sec > 0) %>%
    mutate(position_c = position - mean(position))

  fit <- lmer(log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID), data = model_data)
  emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ vistype, lmer.df = "asymptotic")

  estimates_raw <- as.data.frame(confint(emm, type = "response"))
  estimates_ci <- ci_bounds(estimates_raw)
  estimates <- tibble::tibble(
    vistype = as.character(estimates_raw$vistype),
    estimated_time = estimates_raw$response,
    lower_ci = estimates_ci$lower,
    upper_ci = estimates_ci$upper
  ) %>%
    # Canonical visualization order (audit V1): the levels run bottom to top in
    # the horizontal figures (Basic topoplot at the top); the rows of the table
    # start with Basic topoplot.
    mutate(vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE)) %>%
    arrange(desc(vistype))

  set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
  contrasts_raw <- contrast(
    emm,
    method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
    ref = "basic",
    adjust = "mvt"
  ) %>%
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), type = "response") %>%
    as.data.frame()
  contrasts_ci <- ci_bounds(contrasts_raw)
  contrasts <- tibble::tibble(
    vistype = stringr::str_remove(as.character(contrasts_raw$contrast), " / basic$"),
    ratio = contrasts_raw$ratio,
    lower_ci = contrasts_ci$lower,
    upper_ci = contrasts_ci$upper,
    p_value = contrasts_raw$p.value
  ) %>%
    arrange(match(vistype, vistype_order))  # canonical order (audit V1)

  list(data = model_data, fit = fit, estimates = estimates, contrasts = contrasts)
}

# Short verdict per visualization from the Dunnett-adjusted interval.
contrast_verdict <- function(lower, upper) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    lower > 1 ~ "slower",
    upper < 1 ~ "faster",
    TRUE ~ "not clearly different"
  )
}

format_ratio_ci <- function(ratio, lower, upper) {
  sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", ratio, lower, upper)
}

# One sentence from the Dunnett-adjusted intervals, so the text follows the data.
describe_time_contrasts <- function(contrasts) {
  contrasts <- contrasts %>%
    mutate(
      verdict = contrast_verdict(lower_ci, upper_ci),
      label = sprintf(
        "%s (%s)",
        table_vistype(vistype),
        format_ratio_ci(ratio, lower_ci, upper_ci)
      )
    )
  part <- function(v, text) {
    labels <- contrasts$label[contrasts$verdict == v]
    if (length(labels) == 0) return(NULL)
    paste0(text, knitr::combine_words(labels))
  }
  if (all(contrasts$verdict == "slower")) {
    return(paste0(
      "all six visualizations took longer than Basic topoplot: ",
      knitr::combine_words(contrasts$label)
    ))
  }
  paste0(
    "compared with Basic topoplot, ",
    paste(
      c(
        part("slower", "these took longer: "),
        part("faster", "these were faster: "),
        part("not clearly different", "these were not clearly different: ")
      ),
      collapse = "; "
    )
  )
}

time_contrast_table <- function(contrasts, caption) {
  contrasts %>%
    transmute(
      `Visualization type` = table_vistype(vistype),
      `Ratio to Basic` = sprintf("%.2f", ratio),
      `Lower 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f", lower_ci),
      `Upper 95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f", upper_ci),
      `p (Dunnett-adjusted)` = format_pvalue_html(p_value)
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      format = "html",
      escape = FALSE,
      caption = caption,
      table.attr = kable_table_attributes
    )
}

# Ratios to Basic with their Dunnett-adjusted 95% CIs (audit V8), in the style of
# the Task 1 contrast figure. Log axis (a ratio and its inverse lie equally far
# from 1), limited to the intervals plus the reference line at 1, so no half of
# the plot stays empty when all ratios lie on one side.
# Rows follow the estimate figure above it: the canonical order (audit V1),
# Adjacent plots at the top (there is no Basic topoplot row).
time_contrast_plot <- function(contrasts, estimates) {
  s <- interval_figure_sizes()
  d <- contrasts |>
    mutate(vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(estimates$vistype)))
  range_log <- range(log(c(d$lower_ci, d$upper_ci, 1)))
  pad <- 0.08 * diff(range_log)
  limits <- exp(range_log + c(-pad, pad))
  candidates <- c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.8, 2)
  breaks <- candidates[candidates >= limits[1] & candidates <= limits[2]]
  plot <- ggplot(d, aes(x = ratio, y = vistype)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6, colour = basic_accent) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.14,
      linewidth = s$line,
      colour = "#333333"
    ) +
    geom_point(size = s$point, colour = "#333333") +
    geom_text(
      # Beside the point, on the side away from 1 (clear of the dashed line).
      aes(hjust = side_away_from_zero(log(ratio)), label = sprintf("%.2f", ratio)),
      nudge_y = 0.32,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = s$label,
      colour = "#333333"
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = figure_vistype, drop = TRUE, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    scale_x_log10(
      limits = limits,
      breaks = breaks,
      labels = \(x) sub("\\.?0+$", "", sprintf("%.2f", x)),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = s$axis_y, margin = margin(r = s$margin)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis_x),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank()
    )

  plot /
    basic_axis_caption("Ratio of geometric mean time to", size = s$caption) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.10))
}

time_estimate_table <- function(estimates, caption) {
  estimates |>
    mutate(
      vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
      across(c(estimated_time, lower_ci, upper_ci), \(x) round(x, 1))
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(
      format = "html",
      col.names = c(
        "Visualization type",
        "Geometric mean time, typical participant (s)",
        "Lower 95% CI",
        "Upper 95% CI"
      ),
      caption = caption,
      table.attr = kable_table_attributes
    )
}

time_estimate_plot <- function(estimates, title) {
  ggplot(
    estimates,
    aes(x = estimated_time, y = vistype, colour = vistype == "basic")
  ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.18,
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.1f s", estimated_time)),
      nudge_y = 0.36,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 6
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5), labels = figure_vistype) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = basic_accent),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = \(x) sprintf("%.0f s", x),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Geometric mean time, typical participant (s)",
      y = NULL,
      caption = paste0(
        "Points: back-transformed model estimates (geometric means).\n",
        "Error bars: 95% confidence intervals for each level, not for differences."
      )
    ) +
    plot_theme(base_size = 20) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = rel(1.2)),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "italic"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        colour = vistype_label_colours(levels(estimates$vistype), other = "black")
      ),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(8, 16, 12, 16)
    )
}

time_model_note <- function(position_label = "Presentation position") {
  model_table_note(
    paste0(
      "<ul>",
      "<li><strong>Data:</strong> Trial pages of at most ", time_cap_sec,
      " s (outlier rule at the top of the page).</li>",
      "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Gaussian linear mixed model for log completion ",
      "time: <code>log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID)</code>.</li>",
      "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
      "<li><strong>", position_label, ":</strong> Estimates were calculated at the ",
      "average presentation position.</li>",
      "<li><strong>Estimand:</strong> Back-transformed from log seconds, so each ",
      "estimate is a geometric mean time for a typical participant (participant ",
      "effect at zero), not an arithmetic mean time. Differences from Basic are ",
      "ratios of geometric means.</li>",
      "<li><strong>Intervals:</strong> 95% confidence intervals, asymptotic ",
      "(normal) degrees of freedom.</li>",
      "</ul>"
    ),
    label = "Model details"
  )
}

# ---- Time-accuracy model (Task 1) ---------------------------------------------
fit_time_accuracy <- function(time_model_data) {
  accuracy_data <- time_model_data %>%
    select(ID, vistype, position, position_c, time_sec) %>%
    left_join(
      task1_model %>%
        select(ID, position, correct, pattern, stimulus, wrong_image),
      by = c("ID", "position")
    )

  stopifnot(
    nrow(accuracy_data) == nrow(time_model_data),
    !anyNA(accuracy_data$correct)
  )

  accuracy_data <- accuracy_data %>%
    mutate(log_time = log(time_sec)) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    mutate(
      participant_mean_log_time = mean(log_time),
      log_time_within = log_time - participant_mean_log_time
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      log_time_between_c = participant_mean_log_time -
        mean(participant_mean_log_time)
    )

  fit <- glmer(
    correct ~ log_time_within + log_time_between_c + vistype + pattern +
      position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
    data = accuracy_data,
    family = binomial,
    control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  coefficients <- summary(fit)$coefficients

  effects <- tibble::tibble(
    term = c("log_time_within", "log_time_between_c"),
    comparison = c(
      "Within participants: twice the usual trial time",
      "Between participants: twice the typical completion time"
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      estimate = coefficients[term, "Estimate"],
      standard_error = coefficients[term, "Std. Error"],
      odds_ratio = exp(estimate * log(2)),
      lower_ci = exp((estimate - 1.96 * standard_error) * log(2)),
      upper_ci = exp((estimate + 1.96 * standard_error) * log(2)),
      p_value = coefficients[term, "Pr(>|z|)"]
    )

  list(data = accuracy_data, fit = fit, effects = effects)
}
```

```{r time-data}
#| include: false
# Task 1: pages 5-25 hold trials 1-21; Task 2: pages 29-49 hold trials 1-21.
task1_time_all <- read_page_times("TIME005", "TIME025", 4L, task1)
task2_time_all <- read_page_times("TIME029", "TIME049", 28L, task2)

for (time_data in list(task1_time_all, task2_time_all)) {
  stopifnot(
    !anyDuplicated(time_data[c("ID", "trial")]),
    !anyDuplicated(time_data[c("ID", "position")])
  )
}

task1_time <- apply_time_rule(task1_time_all)
task2_time <- apply_time_rule(task2_time_all)

time_rule_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  task = c("Task 1", "Task 2"),
  trials = c(nrow(task1_time_all), nrow(task2_time_all)),
  removed = trials - c(nrow(task1_time), nrow(task2_time)),
  participants_affected = c(
    n_distinct(task1_time_all$ID[task1_time_all$time_sec > time_cap_sec]),
    n_distinct(task2_time_all$ID[task2_time_all$time_sec > time_cap_sec])
  ),
  iqr_removed = trials - c(
    nrow(remove_group_iqr_outliers(task1_time_all, time_sec, vistype)),
    nrow(remove_group_iqr_outliers(task2_time_all, time_sec, vistype))
  ),
  median_sec = c(median(task1_time_all$time_sec), median(task2_time_all$time_sec)),
  max_sec = c(max(task1_time_all$time_sec), max(task2_time_all$time_sec))
)

pct <- function(x, n) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x / n)
```

## Outlier rule

One rule applies to every table, figure, and model on this page: **a trial page time
above `r time_cap_sec` s (3 minutes) is excluded.**

- **Why a fixed cap.** Each trial is one decision on one page. The median page time is
  `r time_rule_counts$median_sec[1]` s (Task 1) and `r time_rule_counts$median_sec[2]` s
  (Task 2), so a page open for more than three minutes (over ten times the median) most
  likely records an interruption, not time spent on the task. The longest pages lasted
  `r scales::comma(time_rule_counts$max_sec[1])` s and
  `r scales::comma(time_rule_counts$max_sec[2])` s. The cap is fixed in seconds rather
  than estimated from the data, so it does not depend on which visualizations are slow.
- **What it removes.** Task 1: `r time_rule_counts$removed[1]` of
  `r scales::comma(time_rule_counts$trials[1])` trials
  (`r pct(time_rule_counts$removed[1], time_rule_counts$trials[1])`, from
  `r time_rule_counts$participants_affected[1]` participants). Task 2:
  `r time_rule_counts$removed[2]` of `r scales::comma(time_rule_counts$trials[2])` trials
  (`r pct(time_rule_counts$removed[2], time_rule_counts$trials[2])`, from
  `r time_rule_counts$participants_affected[2]` participants).
- **What it replaces.** Earlier versions of this page dropped trials outside 1.5 × IQR
  within each visualization for the descriptive tables only, while the models kept every
  trial. That rule removed `r time_rule_counts$iqr_removed[1]` (Task 1,
  `r pct(time_rule_counts$iqr_removed[1], time_rule_counts$trials[1])`) and
  `r time_rule_counts$iqr_removed[2]` (Task 2,
  `r pct(time_rule_counts$iqr_removed[2], time_rule_counts$trials[2])`) trials, mostly
  ordinary slow trials. The cap was chosen after the time distributions had been seen,
  so both alternatives are reported as [sensitivity analyses](#sensitivity) below.

**What the model estimates are.** The models analyze log time. Back-transformed
estimates are **geometric mean times for a typical participant** (participant effect at
zero) at the average presentation position. They are not arithmetic mean times, which
are larger because time is right-skewed. Differences from Basic topoplot are reported as
ratios of geometric means: a ratio of 1.40 means 40% longer.

*In plain words:* a geometric mean multiplies the times instead of adding them, so a few
very slow trials pull it up much less than an ordinary average. For 5 s, 10 s and 60 s
the ordinary average is 25 s, the geometric mean about 14 s: close to a typical time.

**Multiple comparisons.** The primary comparisons are the six visualizations against
Basic topoplot within each task, with Dunnett-adjusted 95% confidence intervals and p
values (`emmeans` `mvt`, the exact multivariate-*t* adjustment). The same family,
Dunnett-adjusted, is used on the Task 1, Task 2, Hit or miss and rating pages.

*In plain words:* with six comparisons, the chance that at least one ordinary 95%
interval is wrong is about 26%. Dunnett's method widens the six intervals just enough
that all six together are right with 95% confidence. A difference whose Dunnett interval
excludes "no difference" (ratio 1) therefore holds even though six comparisons were made.

## Task 1: comparison

- SoSci Survey records the time spent on each questionnaire **page**. Each Task 1 trial
  has its own page (pages 5–25 hold trials 1–21), and a page keeps its number when the
  display order is randomized. `TIME005`–`TIME025` are therefore the times of trials
  1–21. Each time is linked to its trial, and the presentation position is taken from the
  logged display order.

- The check below plots time by presentation position. With a correct link, the first
  trial a participant sees is the slowest, and times then fall as participants learn the
  task.

::: {.callout-note title="Check: completion time by presentation position" collapse="true"}

```{r task1-time-position-check}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: 'Points: geometric mean of completion time per presentation position. Ribbon: 95% confidence interval (t interval on log time, back-transformed). Log time axis.'
# Geometric mean per position with a 95% t interval, both computed on log time
# and back-transformed; log time axis to match (audit V17).
task1_time %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    log_mean = mean(log(time_sec)),
    log_se = sd(log(time_sec)) / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    geometric_mean = exp(log_mean),
    lower = exp(log_mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * log_se),
    upper = exp(log_mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * log_se)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(position, geometric_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#3182BD", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "#3182BD", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#3182BD", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 21)) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 60, 90, 120),
    labels = \(x) paste0(x, " s")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Presentation position",
    y = "Geometric-mean time (log scale)",
    title = "Times fall as participants learn the task"
  ) +
  # Tick labels near the axis-title size at the display width (audit V2).
  plot_theme(base_size = 17) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = rel(1.2)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16)
  )
```

```{r task1-time-summary}
summarise_observed_time <- function(time_data) {
  time_data %>%
    group_by(vistype) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      median_sec = median(time_sec),
      geometric_mean_sec = exp(mean(log(time_sec))),
      mean_sec = mean(time_sec),
      sd_sec = sd(time_sec),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(order_vistype(vistype)) |>  # canonical order (audit V1)
    mutate(
      vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
      across(c(median_sec, geometric_mean_sec, mean_sec, sd_sec), \(x) round(x, 1))
    )
}

observed_time_columns <- c(
  "Visualization type",
  "Responses",
  "Median (s)",
  "Geometric mean (s)",
  "Mean (s)",
  "SD (s)"
)

task1_time %>%
  summarise_observed_time() |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = observed_time_columns,
    caption = paste0(
      "Observed comparison-task completion time by visualization type ",
      "(trial pages of at most ", time_cap_sec, " s)"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

```{r task1-time-violin}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 6.5
# Horizontal violins (audit V16): labels read without rotation. Rows in the
# canonical order of the time figures below (audit V1), Basic topoplot at the
# top. Log scale: the model works
# on log time, and a raw axis up to the cap would squash the bulk of the
# distribution. Vertical line inside each violin = observed geometric mean.
task1_time_gm <- task1_time %>%
  group_by(vistype) %>%
  summarise(log10_mean = mean(log10(time_sec)), .groups = "drop")
task1_time_violin_data <- task1_time %>%
  mutate(vistype = order_vistype(vistype, top_first = TRUE))

task1_time_violin <- ggplot(task1_time_violin_data, aes(time_sec, vistype)) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    fill = "#6BAED6",
    colour = "#333333",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  # A log axis cannot reach 0. No hard lower limit (the shortest trial is just
  # under 1 s and must stay in its violin); the axis ends just below it, with a
  # tick at 1 s.
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 180))

# Width of each violin at its geometric mean, so the mean line spans the violin.
task1_time_violin_geometry <- layer_data(task1_time_violin, 1) %>%
  transmute(
    row_position = as.numeric(y),
    log10_time = x,
    half_width = violinwidth * width / 2
  )

task1_time_mean_bars <- task1_time_gm %>%
  mutate(row_position = match(as.character(vistype), levels(task1_time_violin_data$vistype))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    half_width = approx(
      x = task1_time_violin_geometry$log10_time[
        task1_time_violin_geometry$row_position == row_position
      ],
      y = task1_time_violin_geometry$half_width[
        task1_time_violin_geometry$row_position == row_position
      ],
      xout = log10_mean,
      rule = 2
    )$y,
    y_start = row_position - half_width,
    y_end = row_position + half_width,
    geometric_mean = 10^log10_mean
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

task1_time_violin +
  geom_segment(
    data = task1_time_mean_bars,
    aes(
      x = geometric_mean,
      xend = geometric_mean,
      y = y_start,
      yend = y_end
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.8,
```

### Association between completion time and accuracy

The following analyses ask whether longer completion times were associated with greater
accuracy. They describe associations and do not establish that spending more time caused
participants to answer correctly. They use the same trials as the time model (pages of at
most `r time_cap_sec` s).

```{r task1-time-accuracy-association}
task1_time_accuracy_results <- fit_time_accuracy(task1_time_model)
task1_time_accuracy <- task1_time_accuracy_results$data
task1_time_accuracy_fit <- task1_time_accuracy_results$fit
task1_time_accuracy_effects <- task1_time_accuracy_results$effects

task1_time_accuracy_counts <- task1_time_accuracy %>%
  count(ID, name = "trials")

stopifnot(
  nrow(task1_time_accuracy_counts) == task1_n_participants,
  all(task1_time_accuracy_counts$trials <= task1_n_trials)
)

task1_participant_time_accuracy <- task1_time_accuracy %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    accuracy = mean(correct),
    typical_time_sec = exp(mean(log_time)),
    mean_log_time = mean(log_time),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task1_time_accuracy_correlation <- cor.test(
  task1_participant_time_accuracy$mean_log_time,
  task1_participant_time_accuracy$accuracy,
  method = "pearson"
)

task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table <- tibble::tibble(
  participants = nrow(task1_participant_time_accuracy),
  correlation = unname(task1_time_accuracy_correlation$estimate),
  lower_ci = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$conf.int[1],
  upper_ci = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$conf.int[2],
  p_value = task1_time_accuracy_correlation$p.value
)

task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table %>%
  transmute(
    Participants = participants,
    `Pearson r` = sprintf("%.3f", correlation),
    `Lower 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", lower_ci),
    `Upper 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", upper_ci),
    `p value` = format_pvalue_html(p_value)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = paste(
      "Participant-level correlation between accuracy and typical",
      "completion time"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Unit:</strong> One record per participant (N = ",
    task1_n_participants,
    ").</li>",
    "<li><strong>Accuracy:</strong> Proportion correct across the participant's ",
    "retained trials (at most ",
    task1_n_trials,
    ").</li>",
    "<li><strong>Typical time:</strong> Mean log completion time, equivalent to the ",
    "log of the participant's geometric mean time.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Interpretation:</strong> The correlation asks whether participants ",
    "who were generally slower were also generally more accurate.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Correlation details"
)

task1_time_accuracy_effects %>%
  transmute(
    Association = comparison,
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.3f", odds_ratio),
    `Lower 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", lower_ci),
    `Upper 95% CI` = sprintf("%.3f", upper_ci),
    `p value (unadjusted)` = format_pvalue_html(p_value)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Adjusted association between completion time and trial accuracy",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>correct ~ log_time_within + log_time_between_c + vistype + ",
    "pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + ",
    "(1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Within-participant effect:</strong> Compares a participant's ",
    "longer and shorter trials.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Between-participant effect:</strong> Compares participants with ",
    "different typical completion times.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Adjustment:</strong> Visualization type, ERP pattern, presentation ",
    "position, participant baseline accuracy, and target- and distractor-stimulus ",
    "difficulty.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Effect scale:</strong> Odds ratios compare a doubling of completion ",
    "time; values above 1 indicate greater odds of a correct response.</li>",
    "<li><strong>p values:</strong> Wald tests of the two time terms, not adjusted ",
    "for multiplicity.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)

# Plain-language descriptions follow the confidence intervals, so the text stays
# correct when the data change.
describe_association <- function(lower, upper, null, more, less, none) {
  dplyr::case_when(lower > null ~ more, upper < null ~ less, TRUE ~ none)
}

describe_time_accuracy <- function(correlation_table, effects) {
  c(
    correlation = describe_association(
      correlation_table$lower_ci,
      correlation_table$upper_ci,
      0,
      "participants who were generally slower were more accurate",
      "participants who were generally slower were less accurate",
      "participants' typical speed was not clearly associated with their accuracy"
    ),
    within = describe_association(
      effects$lower_ci[1],
      effects$upper_ci[1],
      1,
      "a participant's slower trials were more often answered correctly",
      "a participant's slower trials were less often answered correctly",
      "a participant's slower trials were not clearly more or less accurate"
    ),
    between = describe_association(
      effects$lower_ci[2],
      effects$upper_ci[2],
      1,
      "after adjustment, generally slower participants were more accurate",
      "after adjustment, generally slower participants were less accurate",
      "after adjustment, generally slower participants were not clearly more or less accurate"
    )
  )
}

task1_time_accuracy_text <- describe_time_accuracy(
  task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table,
  task1_time_accuracy_effects
)
```

At the participant level, accuracy and typical completion time had a Pearson correlation
of `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$correlation)`
(95% CI
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$lower_ci)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$upper_ci)`,
*p* = `r format_pvalue_html(task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$p_value)`). In the
adjusted mixed model, doubling the time spent on a trial was associated with an odds
ratio of
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[1])` for a correct response
(95% CI `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[1])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[1])`). The between-participant
odds ratio was `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[2])`
(95% CI `r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[2])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[2])`).

In short, `r task1_time_accuracy_text[["correlation"]]`;
`r task1_time_accuracy_text[["within"]]`; and
`r task1_time_accuracy_text[["between"]]`. These are associations, not effects of
time: a harder trial can both take longer and be answered incorrectly more often.

```{r task1-time-accuracy-summary}
task1_time_accuracy_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  analysis = c(
    "Overall participant correlation",
    "Within participants",
    "Between participants (adjusted)"
  ),
  estimate = c(
    sprintf(
      "r = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$correlation,
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$lower_ci,
      task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$upper_ci
    ),
    sprintf(
      "OR = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[1],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[1],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[1]
    ),
    sprintf(
      "OR = %.3f (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)",
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[2],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[2],
      task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[2]
    )
  ),
  p_value = c(
    task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$p_value,
    task1_time_accuracy_effects$p_value
  ),
  summary = paste0(
    toupper(substring(task1_time_accuracy_text, 1, 1)),
    substring(task1_time_accuracy_text, 2),
    "."
  )
)

task1_time_accuracy_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Analysis = analysis,
    `Estimate (95% CI)` = estimate,
    `p value (unadjusted)` = format_pvalue_html(p_value),
    `Plain-language summary` = summary
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Short summary of completion-time and accuracy results",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

## Task 2: detection

- SoSci Survey records the time spent on each questionnaire **page**. Each Task 2 trial
  has its own page (pages 29–49 hold trials 1–21), and a page keeps its number when the
  display order is randomized. `TIME029`–`TIME049` are therefore the times of trials
  1–21. Each time is linked to its trial, and the presentation position is taken from the
  order variables (`A207`).

- The check below plots time by presentation position. With a correct link, the first
  trial a participant sees is the slowest, and times then fall as participants learn the
  task.

- Only non-missing positive times with an identified visualization type and at most
  `r time_cap_sec` s are retained ([outlier rule](#outlier-rule)). The same trials enter
  the descriptive table and the model.

- The model analyzes log completion time because trial times are positive and typically
  right-skewed:

  ```r
  log(time_sec) ~ vistype + position_c + (1 | ID)
  ```

- The participant random intercept allows participants to have different typical response
  speeds. Presentation position adjusts for linear changes in speed across the 21 trials.
  Back-transformed estimates are geometric mean times for a typical participant.

::: {.callout-note title="Check: completion time by presentation position" collapse="true"}

```{r task2-time-position-check}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: 'Points: geometric mean of completion time per presentation position. Ribbon: 95% confidence interval (t interval on log time, back-transformed). Log time axis.'
# Geometric mean per position with a 95% t interval, both computed on log time
# and back-transformed; log time axis to match (audit V17).
task2_time %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    log_mean = mean(log(time_sec)),
    log_se = sd(log(time_sec)) / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    geometric_mean = exp(log_mean),
    lower = exp(log_mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * log_se),
    upper = exp(log_mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * log_se)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(position, geometric_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#3182BD", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "#3182BD", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#3182BD", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 21)) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 60, 90, 120),
    labels = \(x) paste0(x, " s")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Presentation position",
    y = "Geometric-mean time (log scale)",
    title = "Times fall as participants learn the task"
  ) +
  # Tick labels near the axis-title size at the display width (audit V2).
  plot_theme(base_size = 17) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = rel(1.2)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16)
  )
```

## Sensitivity analyses: outlier handling {#sensitivity}

```{r time-sensitivity}
#| include: false
time_rule_labels <- c(
  cap = paste0("Cap at ", time_cap_sec, " s (main)"),
  all = "All trials kept",
  iqr = "1.5 × IQR within visualization"
)

time_rule_datasets <- list(
  "Task 1" = list(
    cap = task1_time,
    all = task1_time_all,
    iqr = remove_group_iqr_outliers(task1_time_all, time_sec, vistype)
  ),
  "Task 2" = list(
    cap = task2_time,
    all = task2_time_all,
    iqr = remove_group_iqr_outliers(task2_time_all, time_sec, vistype)
  )
)

time_sensitivity <- purrr::imap_dfr(time_rule_datasets, \(datasets, task) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(datasets, \(time_data, rule) {
    results <- if (rule == "cap") {
      if (task == "Task 1") task1_time_results else task2_time_results
    } else {
      fit_time_model(time_data)
    }
    results$contrasts %>%
      mutate(task = task, rule = rule, trials = nrow(results$data))
  })
}) %>%
  mutate(verdict = contrast_verdict(lower_ci, upper_ci))

# Does any visualization change its verdict (slower / faster / unclear) vs the main rule?
time_sensitivity_changes <- time_sensitivity %>%
  select(task, vistype, rule, verdict) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = verdict) %>%
  filter(all != cap | iqr != cap)

describe_sensitivity_changes <- function(changes) {
  if (nrow(changes) == 0) {
    return(paste(
      "Every visualization keeps the same verdict (slower than, faster than, or not",
      "clearly different from Basic topoplot) under all three rules"
    ))
  }
  details <- changes %>%
    mutate(text = sprintf(
      "%s, %s: %s with the cap, %s with all trials, %s with the IQR rule",
      task, table_vistype(vistype), cap, all, iqr
    )) %>%
    pull(text)
  paste0(
    "The verdict changes for ", number_word(nrow(changes)), " comparison",
    if (nrow(changes) > 1) "s" else "", " (", paste(details, collapse = "; "), ")"
  )
}

# Time-accuracy associations with all trials kept (old version of the page).
task1_time_accuracy_all <- fit_time_accuracy(fit_time_model(task1_time_all)$data)
task1_time_accuracy_iqr <- fit_time_accuracy(
  fit_time_model(time_rule_datasets[["Task 1"]][["iqr"]])$data
)

time_accuracy_sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  task1_time_accuracy_effects %>% mutate(rule = "cap"),
  task1_time_accuracy_all$effects %>% mutate(rule = "all"),
  task1_time_accuracy_iqr$effects %>% mutate(rule = "iqr")
) %>%
  mutate(
    verdict = describe_association(lower_ci, upper_ci, 1, "positive", "negative", "unclear")
  )

time_accuracy_changes <- time_accuracy_sensitivity %>%
  select(term, rule, verdict) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = verdict) %>%
  filter(all != cap | iqr != cap)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Sensitivity: three outlier rules" collapse="true"}

The main analysis excludes trial pages above `r time_cap_sec` s. Here the time models
are refitted with **all trials kept** and with the previous **1.5 × IQR rule within each
visualization**. Cells show the ratio of geometric mean time to Basic topoplot with its
Dunnett-adjusted 95% CI; bold cells exclude 1.

```{r time-sensitivity-table}
time_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    cell = format_ratio_ci(ratio, lower_ci, upper_ci),
    cell = if_else(verdict != "not clearly different", paste0("<b>", cell, "</b>"), cell),
    rule = factor(rule, levels = names(time_rule_labels), labels = time_rule_labels)
  ) %>%
  arrange(task, rule) %>%
  select(task, vistype, rule, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(task, match(vistype, vistype_order)) %>%  # canonical order (audit V1)
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) %>%
  rename(Task = task, `Visualization type` = vistype) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Ratio to Basic topoplot [Dunnett-adjusted 95% CI] under three outlier rules",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

time_sensitivity %>%
  distinct(task, rule, trials) %>%
  mutate(rule = unname(time_rule_labels[rule])) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = trials) %>%
  rename(Task = task) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Trials entering each model",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

`r describe_sensitivity_changes(time_sensitivity_changes)`.

**Task 1 time–accuracy associations.**

```{r time-accuracy-sensitivity-table}
time_accuracy_sensitivity %>%
  transmute(
    Association = comparison,
    rule = unname(time_rule_labels[rule]),
    cell = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", odds_ratio, lower_ci, upper_ci)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Odds ratio for a doubling of time [95% CI] under three outlier rules",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

`r if (nrow(time_accuracy_changes) == 0) "The direction and clarity of both time–accuracy associations are the same under all three rules." else if (nrow(time_accuracy_changes) == 1) "The verdict of one time–accuracy association depends on the outlier rule; see the table." else "The verdicts of both time–accuracy associations depend on the outlier rule; see the table."`

:::

## Summary of the completion-time results

```{r time-summary-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
# Every number below comes from objects computed above. A visualization is
# called slower or faster only when its Dunnett-adjusted interval excludes 1.
time_summary_task <- function(estimates, contrasts) {
  basic <- estimates |> filter(vistype == "basic")
  verdicts <- contrast_verdict(contrasts$lower_ci, contrasts$upper_ci)
  range_text <- if (all(verdicts == "slower")) {
    sprintf(
      " The visualizations took %.0f%% to %.0f%% longer than Basic topoplot.",
      100 * (min(contrasts$ratio) - 1), 100 * (max(contrasts$ratio) - 1)
    )
  } else {
    ""
  }
  paste0(
    "Basic topoplot took ", sprintf("%.1f", basic$estimated_time),
    " s (geometric mean for a typical participant, 95% CI ",
    sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", basic$lower_ci, basic$upper_ci), "). With Dunnett-adjusted ",
    "intervals (ratio to Basic), ", describe_time_contrasts(contrasts), ".",
    range_text
  )
}

time_summary_slowest <- c(
  task1 = task1_time_contrasts$vistype[which.max(task1_time_contrasts$ratio)],
  task2 = task2_time_contrasts$vistype[which.max(task2_time_contrasts$ratio)]
)
time_summary_all_slower <- all(
  contrast_verdict(task1_time_contrasts$lower_ci, task1_time_contrasts$upper_ci) ==
    "slower",
  contrast_verdict(task2_time_contrasts$lower_ci, task2_time_contrasts$upper_ci) ==
    "slower"
)

time_summary_association_labels <- c(
  log_time_within = "the within-participant association",
  log_time_between_c = "the between-participant association"
)
time_summary_accuracy_changes <- if (nrow(time_accuracy_changes) == 0) {
  "Both time–accuracy associations keep their direction and clarity under all three rules."
} else {
  paste0(
    "The time–accuracy verdict depends on the rule for ",
    knitr::combine_words(sprintf(
      "%s (%s with the cap, %s with all trials, %s with the IQR rule)",
      time_summary_association_labels[time_accuracy_changes$term],
      time_accuracy_changes$cap, time_accuracy_changes$all,
      time_accuracy_changes$iqr
    )),
    "."
  )
}

time_summary_or <- function(i) {
  sprintf(
    "OR = %.2f, 95%% CI %.2f–%.2f",
    task1_time_accuracy_effects$odds_ratio[i],
    task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[i],
    task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[i]
  )
}
```

- **Task 1 (comparison).**
  `r time_summary_task(time_estimates, task1_time_contrasts)`
- **Task 2 (detection).**
  `r time_summary_task(task2_time_estimates, task2_time_contrasts)`
- **Outlier rule.** The main rule removed `r time_rule_counts$removed[1]` Task 1 and
  `r time_rule_counts$removed[2]` Task 2 trial pages longer than `r time_cap_sec` s.
  With all trials kept or with the 1.5 × IQR rule instead:
  `r describe_sensitivity_changes(time_sensitivity_changes)`.
- **Time and accuracy (Task 1).** Within participants, doubling the time on a trial went
  with `r if (task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[1] < 1) "lower" else if (task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[1] > 1) "higher" else "no clear change in the"`
  odds of a correct answer (`r time_summary_or(1)`). Between participants, twice the
  typical time went with `r if (task1_time_accuracy_effects$upper_ci[2] < 1) "lower" else if (task1_time_accuracy_effects$lower_ci[2] > 1) "higher" else "no clear change in the"`
  odds (`r time_summary_or(2)`), and the participant-level correlation was
  *r* = `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$correlation)` (95% CI
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$lower_ci)` to
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_time_accuracy_correlation_table$upper_ci)`).
- **Time and accuracy, outlier rules.** `r time_summary_accuracy_changes`
- **Interpretation.**
  `r if (time_summary_all_slower) paste0("With the main rule, every uncertainty visualization took longer than Basic topoplot in both tasks. ", if (time_summary_slowest[["task1"]] == time_summary_slowest[["task2"]]) paste0(table_vistype(time_summary_slowest[["task1"]]), " was the slowest in both tasks. ") else "") else "Not every visualization differed clearly from Basic topoplot; see the task bullets above. "`The
  time–accuracy results are associations, not effects of time: a harder trial can both
  take longer and be answered incorrectly more often.
